subject: using variable names for column names in summarize

messages.author: 2ec9a7ffb866f600
messages.subject: using variable names for column names in summarize
parts:
I am trying to use the name of a string object as the column on which to summarize. A sample data set is,

 

structure(list(factor = c("CA01PHF", "CA02DNS", "CA02DNS", "CA02DNS",

"CA02DNS", "CA02PHF", "CA03DNS", "CA03DNS", "CA04DNS", "CA04DNS",

"CA04DNS", "CA04DNS", "CB01RCA", "CB01RCA"), value = c(0.417714477466949,

0.90595611336548, -0.0912105279735158, 2.35953643919453, 2.42984912516162,

3.01274616561837, -2.62287846202045, -1.04103370735644, 0.997433783115294,

0.292808410166579, -1.67107734452788, 0.747935650795302, -2.35656465787096,

2.84301978780404)), .Names = c("factor", "value"), row.names = c(492L,

1212L, 1253L, 1352L, 1392L, 493L, 1213L, 1353L, 1214L, 1254L,

1354L, 1393L, 494L, 1045L), class = "data.frame")

 

Using this command I get the proper results,

dataMeans <- ddply(data, .(factor), summarise, total = sum(value))

   factor      total

1 CA01PHF  0.4177145

2 CA02DNS  5.6041311

3 CA02PHF  3.0127462

4 CA03DNS -3.6639122

5 CA04DNS  0.3671005

6 CB01RCA  0.4864551

 

However if I use a string variable instead to represent the column name I get either an error or the total sum rather than the sum by .(factor)

I’ve tried other methods but can’t seem to get it working properly.

stringName <- "value”

> dataMeans <- ddply(data, .(factor), summarise, total = sum(stringName))

Error in sum(stringName) : invalid 'type' (character) of argument

 

dataMeans <- ddply(data, .(factor), summarise, total = sum(data[,stringName]))

 

   factor    total

1 CA01PHF 6.224235

2 CA02DNS 6.224235

3 CA02PHF 6.224235

4 CA03DNS 6.224235

5 CA04DNS 6.224235

6 CB01RCA 6.224235

 

 

 

James Bird

Freescale Semiconductor

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: using variable names for column names in summarize
parts:
Hi James,

Yes, that's right, that doesn't work because of the way "summarise"
works. Briefly, it puts the columns of the sub-data frame into the
namespace, and lets you access them directly, then constructs a new
data.frame with the results. But when you put the name of the column
in a string, it doesn't know how to deal with that extra layer of
indirection. There are ways around it involving parse() and eval(),
but you don't want to use them, trust me. Here's what you want to do,
which is to avoid summarise and just construct a little anonymous
function:

colname <- 'value'
ddply(data, .(factor), function(d) data.frame(total=sum(d[,colname])))

Summarise is just a convenience function, but it's not as powerful as
using arbitrary functions.

-Harlan

Harlan,

Your solution works beautifully. Thank you.
I have had some success in the past with parse() & eval() but it was not very straightforward and did not work in this case.
I will use the anonymous function approach next time.

James
